info.name: Adios.dev API — Core reference
info.description:
# Adios.dev API

Deploy and operate applications, work with source-backed workspaces, manage
domains and object storage, and inspect AI agent sessions through the Adios API.

This collection documents the core customer-facing API. It includes editable
request bodies, resource variables, pagination controls, and illustrative
responses. It is a curated reference, not a dump of every platform route.

## Get started

1. Create an account at [Adios.dev](https://adios.dev) and sign in to the
   [Adios app](https://app.adios.dev).
2. Fork this collection into your own workspace. Import the supplied Production
   environment, or create a private environment containing `base_url`,
   `access_token`, and `team_id`.
3. Set `base_url` to `https://api.adios.dev` without a trailing slash.
4. Obtain a bearer token as described below and set `access_token` in your
   private environment. Set `team_id` to the same team selected in your CLI.
5. Send **Check API health**, then **Get current user**. The latter saves your
   `user_id` in the selected environment. Choose **List workloads** to inspect
   your team's applications.

The companion **Adios.dev API — Quick start** collection contains five read-only
requests that can be run in order. Send requests in the core reference
individually: it contains creates, updates, deletes, email invitations, and
runtime operations.

## Authentication

Protected requests inherit `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` from the
collection. Team-scoped requests send `X-Tenant-ID: {{team_id}}`.

For manual API access, a **team administrator** can use the supported CLI
diagnostic-token flow:

```sh
adios login
adios teams
adios teams switch YOUR_TEAM_ID
adios auth print-token --ttl 15m
```

Install the CLI on macOS or Linux with `brew install adiosdotdev/tap/adios`.
Copy the printed token into your private Postman environment. Diagnostic tokens
expire after 1–15 minutes (the command above requests 15 minutes), cannot be
refreshed, and remain bound to the selected team. Mint a new token when it expires.
Account and team permissions still apply to every request.

The password grant is disabled and password login requires signed requests.
This REST collection does not offer a password-based or one-click Postman OAuth
login. Postman's native MCP integration uses a separate, MCP-scoped OAuth flow
whose tokens cannot call general REST routes. Raw CLI tokens are DPoP-bound
and cannot simply be pasted into Bearer auth; use `adios auth print-token`.
Non-admin users need an authorized bearer credential compatible with their
deployment; this collection does not provision one.

Keep tokens in your private fork/environment. Leave shared values empty and
never publish authenticated response captures or environments containing tokens.
Public health and plan-catalog requests explicitly use **No Auth**.

## Using the reference

- Copy IDs returned by list/create requests into the corresponding environment
  variables, such as `workload_id`, `workspace_id`, or `object_bucket_id`.
  The collection never selects a team or target resource automatically.
- Set `region` from **Get deployment context**, `hostname` to a domain you own,
  and `bucket_name` to a globally unique name before using those examples.
- Optional query parameters appear disabled. Enable the ones you need.
  Generated list routes support `page` (default 1) and `per_page` (default 20,
  maximum 100), with results in `data` and pagination metadata in `pagination`.
- Request descriptions list available fields for generated CRUD operations.
  Replace example values and review resource configuration before sending.
- Bucket uploads use **Body → binary**. Select a local file; do not send a
  multipart form. Downloads can return arbitrary content types.
- Build, deploy, preview, and workflow operations may consume paid resources or
  perform configured external actions. Workspace file/tree reads can hydrate
  source. Runtime actions can require an active subscription.
- Saved response examples are synthetic illustrations derived from the schema,
  not captures from production. Custom routes without a complete response
  contract omit examples rather than presenting an invented payload.

## Responses and troubleshooting

Successful requests return a 2xx status. The collection checks this after each
request. A failed assertion indicates a response to investigate; it does not
validate the entire response schema or prove that a deployment became healthy.

| Status | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | Required values, request body, IDs, and `X-Tenant-ID`. |
| 401 | Missing, expired, or incompatible bearer token. |
| 402 | Subscription or resource entitlement required for the operation. |
| 403 | Team membership, role, resource permission, or token/team mismatch. |
| 404 | Resource ID and active team. |
| 409 | Conflicting resource state or operation. |
| 429 | Wait before retrying; honor `Retry-After` when present. |
| 5xx | Service availability; retain the response for private troubleshooting. |

## Coverage

The core reference covers teams and invitations; workloads, builds, and runtime
status; workspaces, files, previews, and commands; workspace sources and source
artifact reads; workflows; domains; object buckets, objects, and access keys;
gateway routes and security profiles; agent sessions and read-only run/message/
plan/event records; feature planning; webhook configuration; AI model settings;
billing reads; and authorized OAuth connections.

Platform administration, service-to-service credentials, provider callbacks,
browser account flows, internal accounting/execution ledgers,
and advanced agent-catalog/automation operations are outside this edition.
The API specification can contain more routes than this curated reference.

For MCP, use the companion **Adios.dev MCP — Public discovery** collection and
the native MCP HTTP or STDIO connection configurations. The hosted endpoint is
`https://api.adios.dev/v1/mcp`; native MCP setup and its OAuth requirements are
documented separately from the REST collection.

Product information: [adios.dev](https://adios.dev).
